blocks.text: Wetland Delineation for Dyer and Sons

items: Prepared for Sandra Little, Dyer and Sons
Purpose: establish the wetland boundary on the parcel before you build
Client of record: {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}}
Fieldwork commenced {{fact:f:E-2015-001.start}}

blocks.text: What We Are Doing, and Why

items: You need a wetland line drawn before the parcel can be developed.
We draw it to the 1987 Corps of Engineers Wetland Delineation Manual and the regional supplement.
The line rests on three things read on the ground: vegetation, soils, and hydrology.
Once it is walked and surveyed, it becomes the basis for a jurisdictional determination from the Corps.
Angela Williams and Mary Foster walk the parcel and flag the boundary in the field.
At each stretch we record paired sample points, one inside the line and one outside it.
Soils are described at the pit and sediment is logged as we go, not from memory afterward.
John Sanchez leads the technical work and writes the report the determination rests on.
We work the visits around the tides, so the schedule follows the water rather than the calendar.
Flagging is underway across the accessible portions of the parcel.
Data forms are being completed at each paired point as we walk it.
One reach along the channel is being resampled before we commit to a line there.
Nothing is drawn as final until the whole boundary has been walked.
We report what we see at the flag line, not what the map suggests.

blocks.text: What You Get at the End

items: A delineation report that states what was found at each point and why the line sits where it does.
Figures showing the flagged boundary tied to a survey drawing.
A request for a jurisdictional determination, submitted to the Corps on your behalf.
A field record behind all of it that a reviewer can follow years from now.
Finish flagging the remaining boundary.
Bring in the survey crew to tie the flags to a drawing.
Draft the delineation report and the jurisdictional determination request.
Walk the flagged line with you before any of it goes to the agency.
